name_note: The GTDB name Lachnocurva vaginae corresponds to the candidate species Candidatus Lachnocurva vaginae, which earlier publications call bacterial vaginosis-associated bacterium 1 (BVAB1).

sentences.text: Candidatus Lachnocurva vaginae, formerly named bacterial vaginosis-associated bacterium 1, is an as-yet uncultured species of the family Lachnospiraceae found in the human vagina.

That study reports the bacterium is often associated with bacterial vaginosis, and further associated with persistence of bacterial vaginosis after metronidazole treatment, increased vaginal inflammation and adverse obstetrics outcomes.
Genomic and metabolomic evidence presented there suggested the candidate species may metabolize D-lactate, produce trimethylamine and be motile.

A preprint defines bacterial vaginosis-associated vagitypes as vaginal microbiomes with high relative abundance of Gardnerella species, Candidatus Lachnocurva vaginae, or a mixture of multiple anaerobic taxa.
Another preprint counts it among dysbiotic vaginal taxa, reporting that Gardnerella vaginalis correlates more strongly with vaginal pH than those taxa do.
